clue.text: Come out again to gather fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a crop
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone goes back outside to pick fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come back into view, emerging once more.

clue.text: Language used by coarser servants

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rough household staff speak a particular tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Expert is, we hear, put in charge

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a ward is someone in your charge

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is is to be taken by its sound, a buzzing IZ

parts.note: the word is, said aloud, sounds like IZ

explanation.surface: An expert, rumour has it, has been given control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert is' reads like a sentence about a specialist; the comma-fenced 'we hear' shows 'is' is taken by sound, and 'put in' places it inside a person in one's charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is informally someone extremely skilled, an ace at something.

clue.text: Killer's impudence when caught in a crime

indicators.note: caught in says one piece is trapped inside another

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or crime
sass is cheeky impudence

explanation.surface: A murderer's cheek when arrested in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; 'caught in' places the cheek just after the first S of the crime phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially of a prominent person.

clue.text: University lecturers found with joint in circulation

parts.note: in British universities a reader is a senior lecturer ranking just below professor
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Academic staff discovered with a cannabis joint being passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette passed round; it is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication's readership is the body of people who read it, akin to its circulation.

clue.text: Musical Director turned up in case

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is a well-known stage musical

explanation.surface: A conductor of a show turned up for a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses EVITA to ATIVE beneath D.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking an indirect object.

clue.text: Tiring year working in branch

indicators.note: in shows the reworked letters go inside the branch

parts.note: a wing is a branch of an organisation

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An exhausting year spent working at a company branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' suggests a job; it reshuffles the year into EARY, which 'in' sets within the branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearying means exhausting, causing fatigue.

clue.text: Continues, and talks at length

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both carrying on and speaking interminably.

clue.text: Wild mare in picture viewed

parts.note: to picture something is to see it in your mind
saw means viewed

explanation.surface: An untamed horse appears in a viewed picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild mare' is an old name for the playground plank, not a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild mare is an archaic name for the plank that rocks up and down on a pivot.

clue.text: Mistake dropping line suggesting recess

indicators.note: dropping indicates a letter is taken away

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: An error that omits a line hints at a hidden nook.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Queen consort taken round one Egyptian city

indicators.note: taken round says the first piece encloses the next

parts.note: Alexandra was consort of King Edward VII
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A royal wife escorted on a tour of a city in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexandra of Denmark was Edward VII's queen; 'taken round' puts I inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is the great port city founded by Alexander on Egypt's coast.

clue.text: Send back into custody revolutionary fellow captured

indicators.note: captured shows one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A rebel has taken a man prisoner and sends him back to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To remand is a legal term for returning an accused person to custody pending trial.

clue.text: Soldier of fortune in tavern, rude, intoxicated

indicators.note: intoxicated suggests the letters are reeling about drunkenly

explanation.surface: A mercenary is rude and drunk in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intoxicated' rearranges the letters of TAVERN and RUDE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer is one who seeks fortune through risky ventures, as a mercenary does.

clue.text: 'Spectator', or Sunday newspaper?

definitions.meaning: a British Sunday paper, sister to The Guardian

explanation.surface: Two British periodicals are named: the weekly and a Sunday paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is itself a magazine title, steering toward periodicals; here it simply means one who watches.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is a watcher, and The Observer is a long-running British Sunday newspaper.

clue.text: Uncover two-thirds of red meat

indicators.note: two-thirds of means keeping two of the three letters, dropping the last

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: Expose most of a piece of rare meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to uncover or disclose.

clue.text: Song about a leader in Africa is abhorrent

indicators.note: about shows the song wraps round the next piece

parts.note: an anthem is a song of praise

indicators.note: leader in means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A song about an African leader is detestable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is anathema' works as 'is abhorrent', anathema being a thing loathed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anathema is utterly loathed, as an abhorrent thing is.

clue.text: An endless task for presenter

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chore is a task

explanation.surface: A tedious never-ending job for a TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter of a news broadcast.

clue.text: Check on what sounds like costly animal

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain

indicators.note: what sounds like says to take the following word by its sound

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Checking up on an apparently expensive creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an Arctic deer, the animal that pulls Santa's sleigh.

clue.text: Is about to negotiate with models

indicators.note: about shows the first word goes round the next

parts.note: to deal is to negotiate or bargain

explanation.surface: Someone is about to bargain with fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are models of perfection to aim for.

clue.text: Doctor treated Kurd, an alkie

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: A physician treated a Kurdish patient who was an alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a medical case; 'treated' really rearranges the patient and the article into UNKARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkie is slang for an alcoholic, a habitual drunk.

clue.text: Cultivated garden set in rows

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the soil, and the letters, being turned over

explanation.surface: A tilled garden laid out in rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranged means arranged in a line or row.

clue.text: Girl taken on by a posh couple?

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, a posh usage
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A young woman hired by an upper-class pair.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreign woman taken on by a family to help with children.

clue.text: Article attracted boy

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
drew means attracted

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece drew in a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is a common boy's name.

clue.text: Hideous nag lost — no further explanation required

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have lost their way and wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A horribly ugly horse has gone missing, and that says it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the point is understood and needs no more words.

clue.text: Incomplete bathroom fixture causes one to wait

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a bidet is a bathroom fixture

explanation.surface: An unfinished bathroom installation makes someone hang about.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is an old verb meaning to wait or remain.

clue.text: Scottish island, reportedly excellent according to Australian

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: beaut is Australian slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An island in Scotland, said to be great by an Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off western Scotland.

clue.text: Free? Think again!

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to deem is to think or judge

explanation.surface: A question about liberty followed by an order to reconsider.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem is to free, as from captivity or debt, by payment.

clue.text: Covered outhouse to retain warmth

indicators.note: to retain means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
heat means warmth

explanation.surface: A covered outbuilding keeps the heat in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' places the warmth just after the first letter of the outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathed means encased or covered, like a sword in its scabbard.
